points.description: States that a doubly-linked list needs extra space/memory because each node stores an additional (back/previous) pointer.
points.partial_credit: Award 2-3 marks for a vague but related answer, e.g. says it uses more memory or is more complex without linking it to the extra pointer, or mentions the extra pointer without saying it costs space.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying in any wording that a doubly-linked list uses more memory/space because of the extra previous (back) pointer in each node. Part marks if only 'more memory' or only 'extra pointer' is given, or the answer is vague. Give no marks for unrelated disadvantages (e.g. only slower search) with no mention of space or extra pointers; extra remarks do not cost marks.
